name: PORRAZO
description: Porrazo (Parosso, Parear) is a fishing game from Mexico/Southwest USA. Play a card; if it matches a table card, capture it and any cards in ascending sequence. Matching the previous player's card = porrazo (bonus). First to 61 wins.

content.text: Porrazo (Parosso, Parear) is a fishing game from Mexico/Southwest USA. Play a card; if it matches a table card, capture it and any cards in ascending sequence. Matching the previous player's card = porrazo (bonus). First to 61 wins.

Introduced from Mexico to Southwest USA end of 19th century. First reference: Philip Firmin 'Contra Parazzo' (San Francisco Argonaut 1900). C. D. Willard rules (1901). Table Talk (1903), In and Out Door Card Games (1904). USPCC Parosso/Parear 1909-1924.
Standard 52 cards. A (low) to K (high). Suits irrelevant.
52 cards, cribbage board or paper for score.
3 cards each, then play. Repeat until deck exhausted. Once per dealer turn: deal tendido (4 face-up) after a 3-card deal.

items.text: Cards in Excess of 26: 2p/2 teams: card score = excess over 26 (half normal).
No Ace Above King: USPCC: sequences end at K; A always low.
No Ronda Declaration: Claim ronda/rondine after play; no pre-announce.
Tendido Last: Tendido = last 4 of deck; dealer has no choice of when.
